page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-96-lssd is an x86_64 general purpose virtual machine instance equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 372 GB of system memory, providing a balanced memory allocation of approximately 3.88 GB per core. The instance incorporates 3221 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage spread across eight drives. It does not provision GPU hardware accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The compute architecture utilizes dedicated core allocations, preventing noisy-neighbor interference and delivering consistent processing throughput across all threads. The integration of 3221 GB of local NVMe SSD storage affords direct, low-latency disk access that bypasses the latency overhead of network-attached block devices. However, this local array is ephemeral, meaning persistent workloads require external snapshotting or software-defined cluster replication to protect against host-level failures.

Combining high parallel compute capacity with large-scale local flash storage improves resource efficiency for I/O-intensive jobs by reducing storage network transit costs and latency bottlenecks. This server configuration is suited for scale-out distributed databases, real-time analytics engines, big data ETL pipelines, and continuous integration workflows requiring substantial local scratch storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-96-lssd is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 96 dedicated x86_64 virtual CPUs and 372 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. This instance incorporates 3221 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage spread across eight drives, delivering ultra-low-latency scratch disk capabilities directly over the local bus. It does not provision GPU acceleration hardware or complimentary public IPv4 networking. While the local NVMe storage layer provides massive I/O performance advantages over standard network-attached block devices, it remains ephemeral and requires independent data replication mechanisms. With its high vCPU count, balanced memory footprint, and high-throughput local disk subsystem, the c4d-standard-96-lssd virtual machine is suited for I/O-heavy enterprise workloads, distributed transactional databases, large-scale ETL processing pipelines, caching layers, and CI/CD pipelines requiring rapid local file manipulation.
